This website and the visualizations were created as assignments for the **Foundations of Data Science in R** course taught by **Professor Jo Hardin** at Pomona College. 

I audited the class in the fall of 2026 and I absolutely loved the course. I am indebted to Professor Hardin, who gracefully allowed my unusual presence in her classroom. I am also grateful to my students, Ava Santos-Volpe and Ryan (bRyan) Mooney, who insisted that I take this class; they knew I would enjoy it.

The visualizations presented here represent assignments designed for students to learn various data science concepts. Students were free to select the [TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/master/data) datasets to analyze and display. I chose datasets on **Orca Encounters in Puget Sound**, **Dear Abby letters**, and **Palmtrees** to practice different types of graphs.

## TidyTuesday
What is TidyTuesday? A response from AI (Gemini)

TidyTuesday is a weekly data project aimed at the R community, hosted by the **R4DS Online Learning Community** (Data Science in a Box / R for Data Science). 

Every Tuesday, a new dataset is posted on GitHub, usually accompanied by a brief article or chart exploring it. Participants from around the world download the data, analyze it, create data visualizations (most commonly using `ggplot2`), and share their code and plots on social media (primarily on X/Twitter and LinkedIn) using the hashtag **#TidyTuesday**.

### Key Features of TidyTuesday

* **Focus on the "Tidyverse":** The project encourages the use of tidy data principles and packages from the `tidyverse` ecosystem (like `dplyr`, `tidyr`, and `ggplot2`), though participants are free to use any tools or programming languages they prefer.
* **Real-World Data:** The datasets cover a wide variety of engaging, often quirky topics—ranging from historical events and scientific discoveries to pop culture, sports, and environmental statistics. 
* **Learning and Community:** It serves as a low-stakes, supportive environment for beginners and experienced data scientists alike to practice data wrangling, sharpen data visualization skills, and learn from how others approach the same dataset.
